title.narrative: COVID-19: Second Health System Enhancement to Address and Limit COVID-19 under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility

description.narrative:
The proposed loan to the Republic of the Philippines for the Second Health System Enhancement to Address and Limit COVID-19 under the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility (HEAL 2). Under the rapid response component (RRC) of the Asia Pacific Vaccine Access Facility (APVAX), will provide the Government of the Philippines with timely financing for safe and effective vaccine procurement and logistics, based on an agreed list of eligible expenditures. It will supplement the initial support of the Asian Development Bank (ADB) to the government's coronavirus disease (COVID-19) response under the Health System Enhancement to Address and Limit COVID-19 (HEAL) project. HEAL 2 is aligned with three operational priorities of ADB's Strategy 2030: (i) addressing remaining poverty and reducing inequalities; (ii) accelerating progress in gender equality; and (iii) fostering regional cooperation and integration.
The Philippines has met all APVAX access criteria by (i) demonstrating the adverse impact of the COVID-19 pandemic; (ii) completing a needs assessment and a vaccination allocation and prioritization plan, including an incremental medical waste management plan and procurement arrangements acceptable to ADB, with ADB's receipt of a Governor's letter confirming its commitment to implement the plan and ensure compliance with the APVAX vaccine eligibility criteria; and (iii) establishing an effective development partner coordination mechanism with a clear role for ADB

Indicator: (Under TA Facility) VIMS launched (providing data disaggregated by gender, age, and priority group) (OP7.3.3) Status: VIMS was launched in Q2 2021.

Indicator: At least 150 million doses of COVID-19 vaccines procured and delivered to the country (OP1.1.2) Status: 241.97M doses of COVID-19 vaccines have been delivered to the country; 85.6M doses (35.39%) were financed under HEAL2. No vaccines have been procured under HEAL2 AF yet. DOH informed ADB that it is proposing to cancel HEAL2 AF and the uncommitted balance of HEAL2.

Indicator: Gender- and socially inclusive protocol and guidelines on the deployment and administration of vaccines, addressing the specific needs of marginalized women and women in especially difficult circumstances, developed, approved, and disseminated (OP2.3.2) Status: Advisory No. 75 "Vaccination of Pregnant Women with COVID-19 vaccines" was approved on 20 August 2021 to prioritize pregnant women for COVID-19 vaccination. Advisory No.84 "Vaccination of Priority Group A Nationwide” was approved on 6 September 2021. This was to prioritize Group A population (estimated at 24.7 million or 23% of the total population) as the first target group for COVID-19 vaccination. Group A includes prioritizes frontline health workers, people with comorbidities, pregnant women, indigent older persons, remaining older persons and indigent populations, and uniformed personnel. Furthermore, Advisory No. 127 “Guidance on Vaccination of Booster Dose to Pregnant and Lactating Women” was issued 31 January 2022 for booster shots for pregnant and lactating women. In order to reach out most marginalized women and vulnerable population (including people with disabilities, elderly who cannot access to vaccine site), DOH with support from WHO, USAID and ADB TA started community level demand generation and communication initiatives to ensure equity and inclusion in COVID-19 vaccination RESBAKUNA campaign in selected regions. This will continue until March 2023.

There are around 31.2 million unreported/unutilized vaccines (15 million Sinovac and 16 million Pfizer vaccines) which were financed by HEAL2. NVOC reported around 7.6 million doses are still unrecorded and the backlog will be reduced by the end of May. A subsequent email update showed that only around 10.2 million Sinovac doses have not been utilized. The mission requested DOH to prepare a report on those unutilized and unreported vaccines with the proposed actions on how to prevent the expiry ad wastage of these vaccines.
During the April 2022 review mission, DOH informed ADB that there will be no more vaccine procurement. However, DOF has not yet been informed of this DOH decision.
